0._section_summary: The abstract reports a single cross-sectional online study of 215 heterosexual women aged 18-88 examining how body appreciation (positive body image) and appearance dissatisfaction (negative body image) relate to sexual function, satisfaction, and distress while controlling for BMI. Results indicated body appreciation uniquely predicted sexual function, satisfaction, and distress beyond BMI and appearance dissatisfaction; body appreciation did not vary with age and moderated the relationship between age and sexual satisfaction for women with clinically significant sexual function difficulties. 10._section_summary: This Discussion reports a single study of adult women showing that body appreciation uniquely predicted better sexual function, greater sexual satisfaction, and lower sexual distress, beyond BMI and appearance dissatisfaction. Body appreciation did not vary with age but moderated the negative relationship between age and sexual satisfaction (buffering satisfaction among women with high body appreciation), while it did not moderate age-related sexual distress.

13._section_summary: This Limitations and Future Directions section notes that the study used cross-sectional, correlational data and therefore cannot determine causality; the authors call for prospective longitudinal studies to address this. It also states the sample tended to consist primarily of healthy, well-educated, Caucasian women, limiting generalizability and prompting recommendations to include women from the LGBTQ community, diverse cultural backgrounds, and clinical samples in future research. The section highlights cohort effects and potential fluctuations over time as additional concerns for future longitudinal work.
